posts.body_html:
Warning: sappy thank you/you folks complete me message inbound.

My town is small. It's rural. It's quite... uniform. The word that keeps coming to mind is homogenous. Homogenous in appearance, world views, interests. And to be frank, I don't especially fit in well on any front. Don't get me wrong: I have a yin-to-my-yang wife and beautiful family, lots of friends, plenty of things to do. It's not a bad place to be, per say. I am just perpetually "that odd guy that seems really friendly." Many times it would be nice to meet other odd folks in person; to have a meeting of the odd minds on weekends. A group of folks who get me. Though it may seem odd to say this about folks I have never met in "real life," you guys and gals of this forum fit that role.

I think of the previous generation's round-peg-in-square-hole types and feel pity for them. Prior to the electronic mycelium we call the Internet those folks had no way to be who they are and explore and fully appreciate their world. Groups such as this allow this to happen for me and countless others as everyone has mentioned before. This, coupled with seeing everyone here outside of the forum on Facebook and other social media drive the point home: We are eclectic, we might not fit in, but we are definitely not alone. We might have never met in person, but that singularly does not matter. It is the connection of thoughts and motivations--not tactile or visual contact--that make a community.

There is a far greater community in the world now in the twenty-first century than small towns such as mine or even states or countries. There is a global array of communities based on interests and understanding. I am glad that this forum and its users are my community, and every day I am thankful for all of you jokers. It is this connection with each other that truly reduces world suck, in my opinion. Thank you for helping my world--and everyone's world for that matter--suck less.

Part 2- Growing the Forum
Pre-Wang

I made a video advertising the forum, just after Rob joined.

And while Rob was awesome, he just wasn't the forum type.

Sarracenia Addict
to me
Apr 7, 2011Details

Great forum! Looking forward to you "growing" it!

...

I'm not too sure I'd be the right person to give you forum insight/advice as I don't really go on any forums much anymore these days. However -- when I was frequenting the boards, I appreciate the sense of community. I mean, that's what it's for, right? Forums are a great place to learn, to bounce ideas off people, to express ideas, and to grow new ones. I also noticed that each forum has its kind of core "crowd" with it's own flavor, like CPUK, Terraforums... so on. Of course in every community there will be the naysayers....(ex: i just put a link up on the FB page, and all of a sudden, " I don't want to be a buzzkill, but why create another CP forum? I can name 4 off the top of my head in the US alone." )... so that's one thing to take into consideration too is your goals for the forum, the folks you want to reach out to ( I assume more local NYC Sarracenia folk, yes?).

I also like the fact you have Sales/Trades as well. Terraforums, for example does not allow sales, though many other forums do, so that's good.

...
Rob

Yeah, the early days were rough. Here is the post Rob was talking about:


I was looking to connect to other growers, and while Rob helped, his blog and popularity hadnt quite reached what it is today. Mentioning my forum on his FB page didn't do much to the numbers.

His feedback was taken to heart though. Even back then in 2011 Rob realized I wasn't trying to make a normal forum. He said He appreciated the sense of community (a sentiment echoed by many in this thread), and liked that I had a Sales/Trade section.

Mike Joined in December and things began to change.

Early Wang Days 

I feel good posting this quote, as Mike already mentioned that he said this to me:
Michael Wang
to me
Dec 2, 2011Details
Hi Jonathan,

First off, I want to commend you for building the Sarracenia forum! You are a pioneer, and thank you for taking on the challenge!

I'd like to help direct more users to the website by posting some interesting topics. It looks like we have a challenge in attracting more people to the forum, and as you mentioned in one of the posts, the forum is only as good as its participants. To help attract more people, I'll put a few posts with some nice pictures and descriptions, and then try to steer some other folks this way to get the conversations going.


I was just talking to Jerry Addington last night from Washington (you've probably heard of him) and we were discussing how there aren't any Sarracenia forums, but you proved us wrong. Congratulations on your new site, and I look forward to helping you turn this place into a social gathering of like-minded people. The hobby is growing, and this is a great step to bring more awareness.
...
I'll also talk to Robert Co who has his sarracenia blog-see if he can help promote the site by making a few posts.

Cheers!
-Mike


To which my reply was hesitant. I let Mike know that I had tried directing people to the site, but it wasn't working well. That I felt my forum didn't have a wide reach like terraforums because the topic was very narrow, but I took his advice to heart too. He gave me lots of hints and suggestions.

For example:
1. Mike was first to ask for a Sarracenia in the Wild Section. His first post was also in this section here:
sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/30/sarracenia-psittacina-wild-various-forms

2. Mike was the one who suggested splitting the Pics Section into species.

There have been other suggestions after these initial ones, but once they were put through Mike quickly went to work!
Brie paulbarden defalotus swampdonkey stevebooth and mikecpking all joined within a week, and were all within the first 20 people to join the forum. Mike took the forum from 10 to twenty in a week. He was no joke. And I was right behind him, always thinking of ways to make things better. By the way, sidenote- if anyone can get Mikecpking and defalotus to come back to the forum it would be quite awesome.

Mike asked for a section to post pictures of entire collections, of many sarracenia types. I thought about it for 10 seconds and knew I was going to call it Sarracenia Panmixia. In my bio classes in college I learned that panmixia was when every individual in a population had an equal opportunity to mate and breed with any other individual within the population. Many calculations to simulate evolution (by natural selection, sexual selection, bottlenecking) assume a panmixic group. I thought, what a better way to describe an assortment of many plants than the same word that describes the random mating of many individuals. Yeah, my mind is weird.
panmixia- random mating within a breeding population

On top of splitting the pics section into species, I have often gotten requests to split the species into subspecies. Due to many hardships in coding sub sub forums, and I also didn't want there to be too many folders - this has not, and most likely will not occur. Imagine I split rubra into all of its subspecies, and you had a plant that didn't fit any of the subspecies descriptions. Where would you put it? Same with var burkii/rosea? If I split purpurea into purp ven/purp purp/rosea, then there would be pictures of the same entity in two locations. Same problems arose for flava forms which look one way during certain parts of the year, but a different way a different part of the year. So this is why the Pics section stays at the species level.

As the years go by

During the first year, many prominent members joined. These included sunbelle kiwiearl bucky78 sarraceniaobsessed cody jerry addington. YES Jerry managed to get an account, and made ONE POST! By the way- sidenote - if anyone can get Jerry to come back to the forum it would be awesome.
sarracenia.proboards.com/thread/175/new-member-jerry

At the end of year one, we had amassed over 50 people on the forum as members!

Now, the number of accounts are over 400, but some are trolls, and most are VERY NEW members, or old members who no longer log on/post. To give you an idea of exponential growth, about 150 of those accounts have been made within the last year.

The more important numbers to me were the number of guests coming into the forum on a daily basis. This grew steadily and slowly. Today, if you add the number of guests and members coming to view the forum daily, it would be about 450 individuals. I wrote code into the forum to bring up a message to ask people who visit the forum, but dont have accounts, to join. This also occurs when people who have accounts, but don't post, lurk for a LONG TIME. The message pops up asking you to post something.

In the early days it was mostly Mike posting, and mostly Mike advertising. I had many dreams and visions of what I wanted this forum to become. And my dreams are still not acheived. There is a bigger plan for this community, which I hope to share with you soon, and has a LOT to do with the recently made Group Projects section.

But a history of the constant changing, and making projects for the forum will have to wait until another post. I am tired. Part 3 coming soon.
